newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Abidjan dockers end strike, port activity resumes.
newsitem.headline: Abidjan dockers end strike, port activity resumes.

text.p: Dock workers at Ivory Coast's main port of Abidjan have called off their pay strike and work has resumed at the port, union officials told Reuters.
"The various agents have reached agreement in the dispute and work resumed at the port last night," said Toure Vakaba, secretary-general of the maritime workers union CEDERMAR.
An aide in the office of dockers union chief Konate Vasiri confirmed that the strike, which started on Monday, had been called off. There were no details of agreements reached.
An official at SAGA, the bigest maritime transport group in Abidjan said port operations appeared to be smooth.
Shipping sources said on Wednesday they feared the strike could slow cocoa exports end of the month when many exporters ship their cocoa after holding out to see prices.
The port of San Pedro to the west, which like Abidjan handles Ivory Coast's cocoa exports, had not been affected.
Dockers want better pay, on a regular monthly basis, rather than hourly, plus annual bonuses in line with other sector.
